tmvp needs credentials to reach your systems, but the agent never needs to see them. Every secret in `config.yaml` is a *reference* that tmvp's local server resolves; the value stays in the server's memory and is redacted from all output. Pick the source that matches how your team already works — you can mix them per secret.

| Source | Write in config.yaml | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| A `.env` file you already have | `"$dotenv(.env.prod, PGPASSWORD)"` | day one: no new tool, works with existing `.env.<env>` files |
| A process environment variable | `"${DB_PASSWORD}"` (optionally `${NAME:-default}`) | CI, containers, anything that injects env vars |
| Any secret manager command | `"$(op read op://Vault/db/password)"`, `"$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=db)"` | 1Password, cloud secret managers, vault |
| A command that writes a file | `"$file(sec get acme@production:DB_PASSWORD --out ${out})"` | `sec` and other tools that write the value to a file instead of stdout |

```yaml
version: 1
product: acme
envs:
  dev:
    type: dev
    secrets:
      pg_pw: "$dotenv(.env.dev, PGPASSWORD)"
    systems:
      db: { type: postgres, read: { dsn: "host=127.0.0.1 port=5432 dbname=acme user=acme password='${secrets.pg_pw}'" } }
  prod:
    type: production
    secrets:
      pg_pw: "${PROD_DB_PASSWORD}"                              # injected by CI
      ssh_key: "$file(sec get acme@production:SSH_KEY --out ${out})"
    systems:
      box: { type: ssh, host: bastion.internal.example, user: deploy, key: "${file:secrets.ssh_key}" }
      db:  { type: postgres, via: box, read: { dsn: "host=db.internal.example dbname=acme user=readonly password='${secrets.pg_pw}'" } }
```

See [Secret managers](/secrets/managers/) for sec, LastPass, 1Password, Bitwarden, Vault, AWS, GCP, Azure and Doppler.

## `$dotenv(file, KEY)`
- **Path:** `.env.prod` is looked up at the repo root, then next to `config.yaml`; `./x` and `../x` are relative to `config.yaml`; absolute paths, `~/…`, `C:\…` and `\\server\share\…` are used as written. `/` and `\` both work, so one config works on macOS, Linux and Windows.
- **Parsing:** standard dotenv — `export KEY=…`, single or double quotes, trailing `# comments`; the last definition of a key wins.
- **Errors:** a missing file, missing key or empty value is `secret_missing`, naming the file and key, never a value.
- **List what you have:** `tmvp env-keys` prints every `.env*` file's key names (and whether each is set) — never values.
- The value still sits in a plain-text file on disk: an agent that runs `cat .env.prod` can read it. For production, prefer a secret manager (`$file(sec get …)`, `$(op read …)`), or block `.env` reads in your agent's settings.

## `${VAR}` — process environment
Read from the **tmvp server's** environment, i.e. the shell that first started it. After changing a variable, run `tmvp server stop`; the next command restarts the server with the new value. `${NAME:-default}` supplies a fallback.

## Inline commands
A field can also hold a command inline: `password: "$(op read op://Vault/db/password)"`. tmvp turns it into an anonymous secret for that system.

## Checking secrets without seeing them
```
tmvp secrets status          # each slot: ok / missing / invalid, source, when fetched — names only
tmvp secrets reload          # fetch again (after a rotation)
tmvp secrets clear           # forget all cached values
tmvp validate                # rejects literal values in config.yaml
```

## Variables that configure tmvp itself
| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `TMVP_ENV` | default env selector for this shell (`dev`, `prod,staging`, `type:prod`); `-e`/positional selectors override it |
| `TMVP_PRODUCT` | pick a product's config (`~/.tmvp/<product>/config.yaml`) when not inside its repo |
| `TMVP_HOME` | tmvp's state folder (default `~/.tmvp`) |
| `TMVP_SOCKET` | path of the local server's socket (default `$TMVP_HOME/run/tmvp.sock`) |
| `TMVP_IDLE` | how long the background server stays up with no requests (default `30m`) |
| `TMVP_NO_SERVER=1` | run in-process without the background server (slower; no shared connections or cached secrets) |
| `TMVP_AGENT` | name recorded as the caller in the audit log (set automatically for known agents) |
